args.title: plan-deviation-report.docx
args.body:
PLAN DEVIATION REPORT
Bankruptcy Restructuring — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization

Matter: harvey_lab/bankruptcy-restructuring/analyze-counterparty-markup-of-plan-of-reorganization
Deliverable: Plan Deviation Report (plan-deviation-report.docx)

I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This deviation report compares the official unsecured creditors committee's redlined plan of reorganization against the debtor's original plan, using the attached valuation summary, transmittal email, and disclosure statement excerpts, together with the operative base materials, the committee's counterparty markup, the schedules and exhibits, and the controlling deal-team correspondence.

The report identifies each material deviation introduced in the committee's redline, reconciles each against the controlling instructions and the disclosure schedules, and sets out the recommended position for each item.

II. CONTROLLING INSTRUCTIONS

The controlling instruction is the latest message in the deal-team email thread, which supersedes any contrary messaging. Under that controlling guidance:

- The client will CONCEDE the conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.
- Any reduction to the survival period is treated as a WALK-AWAY issue and is not acceptable.

All recommendations below are made consistent with that controlling instruction.

III. DEVIATIONS IDENTIFIED IN THE COMMITTEE'S REDLINE

A. Indemnification Cap — Silent Reduction (NOT ACCEPTABLE; CONFIRM DEBTOR CAP)

The committee's redline silently reduces the indemnification cap from the level set in the debtor's original plan. Because the transmittal email does not flag or explain any reduction in the cap, and because the disclosure statement excerpts preserve the debtor's cap, this change is an unmarked substantive deviation. The cap reduction would materially reduce the debtor's recovery protection.

Recommendation: Reject the cap reduction. Require the committee to restore the indemnification cap to the debtor's original-plan level. The reduction is not referenced in the transmittal email or the disclosure statement and appears intended to pass without scrutiny.

B. Indemnification Basket — Conversion from Deductible to Tipping Basket (CONCEDED)

The committee's redline converts the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket, meaning that once the basket threshold is exceeded the full amount of loss becomes recoverable (rather than only the excess above the threshold). The base materials and the schedules do not present any additional risk from this structural change.

Recommendation: Concede this change per the controlling instruction.

C. Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Carve-Outs for Regulatory Action (NOT ACCEPTABLE)

The committee's redline adds new carve-outs to the definition of Material Adverse Effect for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter. Schedule 3.7 of the disclosure schedules discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that directly intersect these new MAE carve-outs. Adding carve-outs that except precisely the conduct identified in Schedule 3.7 would have the effect of neutralizing the debtor's MAE protection in precisely the scenario most likely to arise, while the disclosure statement excerpts do not reflect any narrowing of the debtor's MAE standard.

Recommendation: Reject the new MAE carve-outs. Reconcile the deviation against Schedule 3.7: because the carve-outs are drawn to cover the two pending regulatory inquiries, accepting them would strip the debtor of protection on identified live risks. The carve-outs should be removed and the debtor's original MAE definition restored.

D. Limitation Period / Survival — Shortening for Core Representations (WALK-AWAY; NOT ACCEPTABLE)

The committee's redline shortens the limitation period and thereby reduces the survival period for the core representations. This directly contradicts Exhibit B of the schedules and exhibits, which sets the survival matrix for the transaction. Under the controlling instruction, any reduction to the survival period is a walk-away issue and is not acceptable.

Recommendation: Treat this as a walk-away item. Do not accept any reduction in the survival period for the core representations; the survival matrix in Exhibit B must be preserved as set forth in the debtor's original plan.

E. Retained Liabilities — Silent Shift via Indemnification Changes (NOT ACCEPTABLE)

Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the committee's indemnification changes would silently shift. The combination of the reduced cap and the basket/indemnification changes operates to transfer a class of retained liabilities identified on Schedule 5.2 back to the debtor without any corresponding disclosure or compensation. Because Schedule 5.2 controls over general statements in the base materials, and because the committee's changes do not preserve the Schedule 5.2 allocations, this deviation must be rejected.

Recommendation: Reject the silent shift of Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities. Require that the retained-liability allocations set forth on Schedule 5.2 be preserved in full and that any change to the indemnification regime not alter those allocations.

IV. RECONCILIATION AGAINST SCHEDULES AND EXHIBITS

The disclosure schedules control over general statements in the base bankruptcy restructuring materials:

- Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries): intersects and is adversarially affected by the committee's new MAE carve-outs. (See III.C.)
- Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities): would be silently shifted by the committee's indemnification changes. (See III.E.)
- Exhibit B (survival matrix): contradicted by the committee's shortened limitation period. (See III.D.)

V. RECOMMENDED POSITIONS — SUMMARY TABLE

| # | Deviation | Position |
|---|-----------|----------|
| 1 | Indemnification cap silently reduced | Reject — restore debtor's cap |
| 2 | Basket converted from deductible to tipping | Concede (per controlling instruction) |
| 3 | MAE carve-outs added for regulatory action (Schedule 3.7) | Reject — remove carve-outs |
| 4 | Survival / limitation period shortened (contradicts Exhibit B) | Walk-away — not acceptable |
| 5 | Retained liabilities silently shifted (Schedule 5.2) | Reject — preserve Schedule 5.2 |

VI. CONCLUSION

The committee's redlined plan contains five material deviations from the debtor's original plan. Of these, one is conceded (the basket conversion), while the remaining four — the reduced indemnification cap, the new MAE carve-outs, the shortened survival period, and the shift of Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities — are not acceptable and should be rejected. The survival-period reduction in particular is a walk-away item under the controlling instructions, and it directly contradicts Exhibit B's survival matrix.

The deviations were identified and reconciled using the attached valuation summary, transmittal email, and disclosure statement excerpts, and against the controlling deal-team correspondence, the disclosure schedules, and the base materials. This report should be used to direct the response to the committee's redline.

Prepared by: Bankruptcy Restructuring Practice
Deliverable: plan-deviation-report.docx
